verdicts.note: Read tests/test_boot_deferred_init.py 1-49: one brace extractor plus substring/regex asserts on src/dash_main.c, nothing compiled. compile.yml has 213 'python3 tests/' lines and none names this file; no glob or discover runner exists in workflows, scripts or Makefiles. grep 'boot_deferred' over the repo (excluding .git): only the comment at tests/test_dashboard_console_summary.py:36.

grep '^def (function|extract|fn|func|body|c_function)\(' over tests/*.py gives 110 files. Re-read all 17 cited ranges; every range is exact (cloud_history_browser 17-46, cloud_recovery 19-46, cloud_upload_ledger 19-44 are the literal-aware variants) and the 16 in-unit ranges sum to 182 lines. Net saving must also pay for the sys.path.insert plus import lines each file would gain (about 2 per file), so ~110 net in this unit, which is >= 80 lines and therefore rank 3 on the scale, not 2.

corrected.benefit: ~110 net lines in this unit (182 cited lines, minus ~30 for the shared module and ~2 import lines in each of 16 files), MEASURED from ranges; roughly 550 more repo-wide (~94 further files x ~6 net lines), INFERRED.

verdicts.note: Re-read every cited line; all nine are self-name asserts as described. But the list is incomplete: grep for '"python3 tests/<own name>.py" in workflow' over tests/*.py finds nine more files with the same self-assert. grep -cw workflow per file shows that in 15 of the 18 files (all except ps2ips_rpc and rolling_release_workflow) the compile.yml read is used only by this assert, so the read line goes too. Total ~33 lines (18 asserts + 15 reads), >= 15 lines, so rank 2.

corrected.problem: Eighteen tests assert that the string 'python3 tests/<this file>.py' appears in compile.yml. When CI runs the test the line is necessarily there, so the assert can only fire when someone runs the file by hand after removing it from the workflow. In 15 of these files the compile.yml text is read only for this assert.
corrected.fix: Delete the self-referencing asserts, and the compile.yml read in the 15 files where nothing else uses it.
corrected.benefit: ~33 lines removed and one file read per run in 15 tests (MEASURED: 18 assert lines plus 15 read lines; grep -cw workflow is 2 in those 15 files).
corrected.evidence: grep '"python3 tests/<own name>.py" in workflow' for every file containing 'in workflow': 17 hits (cloud_upload_ledger, dash_card_tool, loader_linkfile, mc_card_write, mc_fingerprint, mc_ps1_card, mc_save_export, mc_save_formats, mmce_dread_returns, mmce_exclusive_new_files, mmce_fingerprint_backup, mmce_fs_restore_guard, mmce_handle_release, mmce_save_versions, mmce_selectable_install, ps2ips_rpc, rolling_release_workflow) plus the inline form in test_dash_pause.py:22. grep -cw workflow: 2 in all of them except ps2ips_rpc (3) and rolling_release_workflow (18).

verdicts.note: Read tests/test_copy_pipeline.py 16-20 and tests/test_copy_short_io.py 54. grep of the seven helper names over the repo (excluding .git) hits only those lines. The three extra strings (LS-COPY-, LS-OLD-, FIO_O_EXCL) guard against reintroducing the superseded #187 temp/rollback protocol (docs/plans/2026-10-19-zack-issues.md:4, commit dfb62bf 'Restore upstream R3Z direct file overwrite'); line 17 already pins the exact open flags, so dropping the loop loses little. Ratings fit.

The premise that the cited blocks 'restate code already compiled and run by the same file' does not hold: sync_tree and drive_upload_file (cloud_upload_ledger 50-62), cloudBrowseHistory (cloud_history_browser 57-64), cloudLink (cloud_link_screen 60-69) and every dash_browser.c check in test_dash_card_tool (25-28, 433-436, 1215-1217, 1408, 1411-1412) are absent from the harness extraction lists (cloud_upload_ledger 65, cloud_history_browser 83, cloud_recovery 164-167), and the ps2.yaml/embed_blobs.S checks (bgm_sidecar 21-24) are build wiring. Those are exactly the 'wiring points the harness cannot reach' that the fix itself says to keep, so the location list contradicts the fix and the ~50-line saving is unsupported. cloud_recovery.py:62 is an intentional implication (if the source says Drive files are not deleted, it must not issue DELETE), not a broken check. test_cloud_relay.py (read 1-26) is cheap and guards that the relay never uses rclone sync, which would delete remote backups; deleting a data-loss guard is not a net win.

Read tests/test_cloud_tls_paths.py 1-67 and scripts/build_cloud_tls.sh:42-52. The description is right: lines 22-65 compile a test-written file and re-implement the script's quote escaping in Python at 59. But the loop at 28-42 runs two compiles per iteration for two iterations plus one at 60-63, so five host compiles, not four. 44 lines is >= 15, so rank 2.

corrected.benefit: 44 lines removed and five host compiles per CI run (MEASURED: 2 iterations x 2 compiles at 36-40 plus one at 60-63).

verdicts.note: Read test_copy_pipeline.py 38-138 and test_copy_psu_listing.py 54-190. Defines 41-83 match 57-102 except DVRP (65) and the FIO_S_IS* forms (76-77 vs 93-96). The static state lines 88-94 vs 109-115 also match, and the listed one-line stubs (Timer, getIopResetGeneration, waitUntilTimer, drawMsg, readpad, DashIsActive, nonDialog, isPcCardCfPath/Online, ensureMemoryCardPortAccessible, makeHostPath, filerDirReadComplete, genFixPath, genGetStat) are the same. ~45 net lines is >= 15, so rank 2, not 1.

The test_clock_save_action.py part is wrong. dash_settings.c:2432-2435 shows failedSaves() also counts CNF and NET failures, while settingsSaveSoftwareClock (2526-2543) checks only dashStoreSettingsFailed(). Lines 59-60 set unrelated_failed and expect the clock save to succeed. That is a deliberate guard: if the function ever switched to failedSaves(), the stub would return 1 and line 60 would fail. The stub carries __attribute__((unused)) because it is not called today. The test_dash_card_tool.py part holds. _whole (275) is never read and calls saves(B) twice, each a lister subprocess (73-83). browser (25) is never reassigned, so the _br re-reads at 433 and 1411 are redundant. F and G at 449/458 repeat the values set at 280/287.

corrected.title: Redundant code in test_dash_card_tool.py: unused _whole, repeated dash_browser.c reads and F/G reassignments
corrected.problem: _whole (275) is never read, yet it runs the saves() helper, and with it the card lister subprocess, twice. Lines 433 and 1411 re-read src/dash_browser.c into _br, although line 25 already holds the same text in browser and nothing reassigns it. Lines 449 and 458 reassign F and G to the values set at 280 and 287.
corrected.fix: Delete test_dash_card_tool.py:275, 449 and 458. Use browser instead of _br at 434-436 and 1412, and delete lines 433 and 1411.
corrected.benefit: 5 lines removed and two lister subprocess runs per test run (MEASURED: line 275 calls saves(B) twice).
corrected.evidence: grep '_whole|_br|^F =|^G =|dash_browser.c' in test_dash_card_tool.py: _whole only at 275; browser read at 25 and never reassigned; _br at 433 and 1411; F at 280/449 and G at 287/458 with identical values. saves() at 73-83 runs the lister through subprocess.run.

verdicts.note: Read test_copy_short_io.py 1-15 and 95-98, test_cursor_sound_ticks.py 1-25 and test_launch_driver_messages.py 1-26. The argv/git-show mode is as described. compile.yml lines 67, 227 and 228 pass no argument, and the mode skips the seek checks at 95-98. However, the claim that no doc mentions the mode is wrong: the docstrings at test_cursor_sound_ticks.py:8 and test_launch_driver_messages.py:10, which are cited locations, document it as a way to run the checks against an older revision. It is a documented manual option that CI never uses, not an undocumented one.

corrected.problem: These tests read sources through 'git show <argv[1]>:path' when given an argument, so that the checks can run against an older revision. Only the tests' own docstrings document this (test_cursor_sound_ticks.py:8, test_launch_driver_messages.py:10). compile.yml runs all three with no argument (lines 67, 228, 227). In test_copy_short_io.py the mode also silently skips the seek checks at 95-98.
